title: Performance garden: standup notes & action log (2026-12-21)
content:
Meeting: Performance Garden weekly standup (focused on recent tail-latency regressions)
Date: 2026-12-21
Facilitator: Priya Nair
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Priya Nair, Marcus Li, Sofia Alvarez, Jamal Thompson, Hannah Park, Kyle Moreno (observability)

Quick summary:
- New noise in 99.9/99.99 percentiles observed during mixed short/long seq shadow runs last 48h. Not visible in median/95th.
- Correlation signal: bursts align with NVMe GC cycles on some Dedicated hosts and with a small cohort of multi-model ensemble requests.
- We ran targeted shadow experiments (alpha cohort) and a KV-cache eviction tweak; preliminary numbers show reduced 99.9 but increased 95th in a separate path — tradeoff needs exploration.

Data snapshot (representative):
- Baseline (2026-12-18 steady run): p50=12ms, p95=42ms, p99=120ms, p99.9=420ms
- Regression window (2026-12-20 peak): p50=13ms, p95=45ms, p99=125ms, p99.9=980ms (spikes clustered every ~7-9 minutes)
- Latest run (kv-evict-ttl-lower): p50=13ms, p95=48ms, p99=118ms, p99.9=210ms
Notes: p99.9 improvement concurrent with bump in p95 likely due to reduced cache hit contiguity (more cache churn).

Recent runs and configurations run by QA team:
- shadow-run-mix-2026-12-20: 1k req/s mixed seq (short 8–16 tokens, long 512–1024 tokens), model: redwood-v1-7B-fp16, dedicated pool: a100-80gb-6nodes, sampling: 10% traffic
- kv-evict-ttl-lower: mess with prefix-KV eviction threshold (ttl 15m -> 5m) + aggressive local LRU aging
- nvme-isolate-check: pinned dataset on host with NVMe firmware v4.2.1 vs v4.3.0 to check GC alignment
- client-pacing-50ms: introduced client-side pacing jitter to spread bursts

Hypotheses discussed:
1) NVMe GC/compaction introduces short I/O stalls that propagate to tail for workloads that fetch or write cache shards during inference (esp. multi-model ensembles).
2) KV-cache eviction policy currently creates synchronized evictions across shards when requests have similar prefixes, causing temporary cache miss storms.
3) Sequencer/backpressure tuning: a narrow window in our sequencer batching logic will cause opportunistic large batches that create head-of-line microbursts for small requests.
4) Observability sampling bias: our tracing sampler under-samples the long-tail events; so spikes may be noisier than the underlying problem.

Evidence and notes against each hypothesis:
- Hypothesis 1: strong alignment of spike timestamps with NVMe GC logs on 3 hosts during the window. Reproduced with manual GC trigger (nvme-cli forced compile) -> small latency bump but smaller than observed.
- Hypothesis 2: shadow run with staggered TTL (kv-evict-ttl-lower) reduced 99.9 by ~60% but bumped p95 by 6% — consistent with more cache churn but fewer rare huge misses.
- Hypothesis 3: we observed large batch formation in logs around the same times as spikes; correlates with request inter-arrival histograms from client-pacing-50ms run.
- Hypothesis 4: we need higher fidelity sampling on the sidecar for 24h window; current 1/500 trace sampler misses many cold-path evictions.

Immediate action items (owners & due dates):
- Marcus Li: run nvme firmware rollback experiment on isolated pool (hosts: ded-gpu-03..05) and schedule controlled GC triggers; compare 24h histograms. Due: 2026-12-24.
- Sofia Alvarez: iterate on KV eviction policy: implement randomized stagger (jitter eviction window per shard) and run ramped shadow with same traffic mix. Add metrics: per-shard miss-rates and eviction storms. Due: 2026-12-23.
- Jamal Thompson: instrument sequencer to emit batch-formation trace annotations (size, time-to-fill) and create alert on >3x expected batch size within 30s. Deploy to canary. Due: 2026-12-22.
- Hannah Park: increase tracing fidelity for cold-path (sample 1/50) for 48h on alpha shadow cohort; coordinate storage retention for traces. Due: 2026-12-23.
- Priya Nair: run synthetic client-pacing experiments to sweep pacing jitter [0,10,25,50,100ms] and plot p50/p95/p99/p99.9 tradeoffs. Collate into summary. Due: 2026-12-27.
- Kyle Moreno (observability): add transient dashboard tile for NVMe GC events overlayed on tail latency; hook logs->metrics mapping. Due: 2026-12-24.

Short-term mitigations discussed (we can flip fast):
- Route multi-model ensemble traffic to a warmed pool with adjusted cache TTL (config: pool:ensemble-warm, kv_ttl=20m) — canary today at 5% traffic.
- Enable client-side pacing by default for internal test harnesses (via feature flag) to smooth arrival during peak lab runs.

Open questions / research items:
- Why does NVMe forced compaction not fully reproduce the amplitude we saw in the wild? Are there coordinated background tasks (OS-level or telemetry) that compound latencies?
- Can we model cache churn analytically to predict p95 vs p99.9 tradeoffs depending on TTL and shard count? (ask research team for small paper)
- Is there a cheaper kernel-level I/O tweak (io_uring flags, blk-mq tuning) that buys us headroom without hardware changes?

Decisions made in meeting:
- Prioritize non-invasive mitigation: staggered/ randomized KV eviction + sequencer instrumentation.
- Do not change production TTLs for user traffic until shadow results are stable.

Notes for post-run analysis (what to capture):
- Full timeline of 24h with: request histogram, per-shard kv hits, NVMe SMART logs (compaction timestamps), sequencer batch sizes, sidecar CPU/rtc stalls.
- Capture an aligned trace set (sample=1/50) for 30m surrounding any spike detected; keep those traces 30d.

Appendix: experiment commands (copied for reproducibility)
- Shadow run command (internal): 
  ./bench/shadow_run --config configs/mixed_short_long.yaml --qps 1000 --duration 7200 --shadow-rate 0.1 --model redwood-v1-7B-fp16 --pool ensemble-warm

- KV eviction local tweak (dev env): 
  cfg.kv.eviction_policy = "lru_staggered"
  cfg.kv.eviction_jitter_ms = 120000  # 2 minutes jitter per shard
  cfg.kv.ttl_seconds = 300

- Sequencer trace flags (canary): 
  SEQUENCER_TRACE_BATCH=true SEQUENCER_BATCH_NOTIFY_MS=10

Next sync: 2026-12-23 10:00 PT (short check-in to review NVMe rollback & kv-staggered shadow results)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the "garden" metaphor — helps productize the weekly growth of small fixes.
- Log any abnormally timed maintenance windows from cloud provider in the same timeline to avoid chasing ghosts.

End of notes.
summary: Weekly standup capturing investigation into rare tail spikes observed in mixed workload shadow runs. Primary leads: NVMe GC alignment, KV-cache eviction storms, and sequencer batch formation. Action items assigned with short deadlines for targeted experiments and higher-fidelity traces. Next check-in 2026-12-23.
